paragraphs: The STM32 Blue Pill is a popular development board for microcontrollers based on the ARM Cortex-M3 architecture. It features a 72 MHz ARM Cortex-M3 processor, which is ideal for applications requiring high processing power and real-time capabilities. The STM32F103C8T6 microcontroller is the primary component of this board, offering 64 KB of flash memory and 20 KB of SRAM, providing ample resources for software development and data storage. The board also includes a 12-bit ADC for soil moisture measurement and a Timer PWM module for controlling active buzzer alerts. Additionally, it features an onboard indicator LED that turns on automatically when the plant needs watering. The ST-Link V2 In-Circuit Programmer is included to facilitate firmware flashing and debugging of the STM32 microcontroller.

The architecture of the STM32 Blue Pill is based on a 64-bit ARM Cortex-M3 processor, which allows for efficient execution of software applications. The processor has a clock speed of 72 MHz, providing sufficient processing power for real-time tasks such as soil moisture monitoring and active buzzer alerts. The microcontroller also features a 12-bit ADC, which can measure the moisture content of the soil with high accuracy.

The memory of the STM32 Blue Pill is divided into two sections: flash memory and SRAM. Flash memory provides a large amount of storage space for storing programs and data, while SRAM is used for temporary storage during execution. The 64 KB of flash memory allows for the installation of multiple applications and data structures, while the 20 KB of SRAM provides enough space for local variables and temporary calculations.

The peripheral capabilities of the STM32 Blue Pill include a 12-bit ADC for soil moisture measurement, which can be used to monitor the moisture content of the soil in real-time. The Timer PWM module can be used to control active buzzer alerts, which can be triggered when the moisture level falls below a certain threshold.

The operational parameters of the STM32 Blue Pill include an operating voltage of 3.3V, which is suitable for most microcontroller applications. The board also features a ST-Link V2 In-Circuit Programmer, which allows for easy firmware flashing and debugging of the STM32 microcontroller.
